question.text: How many US banks will fail in November or December 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the number of United States bank failures that occur after October 31, 2026, and before January 1, 2027.
question.fine_print: The source for this question will be the [FDIC Failed Bank List](https://www.fdic.gov/bank-failures/failed-bank-list). No other source will be used.

# US bank failures in November-December 2026: research notes

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-09-25: The FDIC Failed Bank List was last updated September 25, 2026. Its newest entry is Nano Banc (Irvine, CA), acquired by Sunwest Bank. The list shows six failures in 2026: Metropolitan Capital Bank & Trust (Jan 30), Community Bank and Trust - West Georgia (May 1), Kentland Federal S&L (Jul 10), Small Business Bank (Jul 17), Tioga-Franklin Savings Bank (Aug 21) and Nano Banc (Sep 25). There were two failures in 2025 (Jan 17 and Jun 27). [FDIC](https://www.fdic.gov/bank-failures/failed-bank-list)
- 2026-10-01: The FDIC's liquidation-listing notice names only Nano Banc in that update. [regulations.gov](https://www.regulations.gov/document/FDIC-2026-1882-0001)

## 2. Current status
- 2026-10-28: Nothing has happened yet that counts. The window opens November 1, and I found no failure dated after September 25. October has had no reported failures, but October failures would not count anyway.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-27: The Fed was expected to hold at 3.75-4.00% at its October 27-28 meeting, with a December hike possible (Citi forecasts one). Brent crude was near $117. [am730](https://www.am730.com.hk/article/1060661), [elEconomista](https://www.eleconomista.es/mercados-cotizaciones/noticias/14023645/10/26/la-fed-se-guarda-la-subida-de-los-tipos-para-diciembre-pese-a-la-presion-de-la-inflacion.html)
- 2026-09-28: Nano Banc was the sixth failure of 2026 and the largest of the year (about $736M in assets, estimated DIF cost about $114M). [24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/09/28/small-california-bank-becomes-the-6th-u-s-bank-to-fail-this-year-sunwest-bank-assumed-all-deposits/), [Daily Hodl](https://dailyhodl.com/2026/09/27/california-bank-abruptly-shuttered-in-sixth-bank-failure-of-2026/amp/)
- 2026-08-25: In the Q2 2026 Quarterly Banking Profile, the Problem Bank List fell by a net 7 to 47 banks. Quarterly industry net income was $90.1B and the Deposit Insurance Fund stood at $161.1B. I only saw this in the ABA Journal, not the FDIC's own report. [ABA Banking Journal](https://bankingjournal.aba.com/2026/08/quarterly-banking-profile-banking-net-income-90-1b-in-q2-2026/)
- 2026-08-21: Tioga-Franklin was the fifth failure, the most in a year since 2023. [Banking Dive](https://www.bankingdive.com/news/tioga-franklin-philadelphia-fifth-bank-failure-2026-second-federal/828591/), [American Banker](https://www.americanbanker.com/news/fifth-bank-fails-in-2026-as-drip-of-small-bank-closures-continues)
- Commentary describes the 2026 failures as a steady drip of small, idiosyncratic closures, not a systemic wave like 2023. [CryptoSlate](https://cryptoslate.com/six-us-banks-have-failed-in-2026-but-the-numbers-look-nothing-like-2023/)

## 4. Base rates
- 2026 pace: six failures in about nine months, roughly 0.67 a month. At that rate, a two-month window would average about 1.3. The pace has picked up: four failures came between July and September, about 1.3 a month. Failures have been spaced 1 to 8 weeks apart (Jul 10 to Jul 17, Jul 17 to Aug 21, Aug 21 to Sep 25).
- November-December failures in past years. These are recalled from the FDIC list, not freshly re-checked, so please verify:
  - 2017: 0
  - 2018: 0
  - 2019: 1 (City National Bank of NJ, Nov 1)
  - 2020: 0
  - 2021: 0
  - 2022: 0
  - 2023: 1 (Citizens Bank, Sac City IA, Nov 3)
  - 2024: 0 (the last failure was Oct 18)
  - 2025: 0
- That is 2 of the last 9 years with exactly one failure, and none with two or more. However, none of those years matched 2026's pace of six failures by September. 2023 had 5 for the full year, and 2019 and 2020 had 4 each.
- Failures usually happen on Fridays. The window has about nine Fridays: Nov 6, 13, 20 and 27, and Dec 4, 11, 18 and 25 (Dec 25 is Christmas, so effectively unlikely).

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket, "US bank failure by December 31, 2026?": Yes at 0.74 (fetched 2026-10-28). Six failures have already happened this year, so this price only makes sense if this market's window starts later, perhaps after Sep 25 or in October. I could not confirm its start date. An earlier series market opened 2026-07-20 shows over 99% (it was presumably triggered by the August or September failures). Do not assume the 0.74 market matches the Nov 1 to Dec 31 window. [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/us-bank-failure-by-december-31-2026-20260720194747677)
- Manifold, total failures in 2026 (six so far):
  - 7 or more: 51%, which implies roughly 51% chance of at least one more failure by Dec 31. That includes any in late October.
  - 8 or more: 31%
  - 9 or more: 15%
  - 10 or more: 16%, which is inconsistent with the 9+ market and suggests thin trading.
  - [Manifold 7+](https://manifold.markets/bessarabov/will-7-or-more-us-banks-fail-in-202-dLQps0QyuE), [8+](https://manifold.markets/bessarabov/will-8-or-more-us-banks-fail-in-202-ztANdUl5CU)
- I found no Kalshi market or expert forecast on the number of failures.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-10-28: FOMC decision. A December hike would add pressure on banks heavy in commercial real estate or securities.
- 2026-10-30: The last Friday in October. A failure that day would not count, but it would change the Manifold "7+" picture.
- 2026-11-03: US midterm elections.
- Late November 2026 (date not confirmed): The Q3 2026 Quarterly Banking Profile, with an updated Problem Bank List count.
- 2026-12-08 to 12-09 (expected): Final FOMC meeting of 2026, where a hike is possible.
- Holidays: Nov 11 (Veterans Day) and Nov 26 (Thanksgiving). [LaRepublica](https://larepublica.pe/latinos-en-usa/2026/10/27/confirman-cierre-masivo-de-bancos-en-estados-unidos-todas-estas-sucursales-cerraran-en-estas-fechas-de-noviembre-295218)

Other sources: [Banking Dive (first failure)](https://www.bankingdive.com/news/chicago-bank-metropolitan-capital-fails-fdic-first-independence-detroit/811119/), [American Banker list](https://www.americanbanker.com/list/15-most-recent-bank-failures), [DEV Community roundup](https://dev.to/specstream/fdic-failed-bank-list-2026-six-banks-closed-this-year-and-the-25-latest-as-a-list-you-can-sort-4e80), [marketintellabs](https://marketintellabs.com/research/bank-failures-2026)

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** The window runs November 1 to December 31, 2026, about nine weeks. The outcome is known on about January 1, 2027.

(b) **Status quo:** No failure has occurred since September 25, and none counts yet. If nothing changed, the answer would be 0.

(c) **Base rates:**
- In November-December of 2017-2025, 7 of 9 years had 0 failures, 2 had exactly 1, and none had 2 or more.
- Those years ran at a much lower annual pace than 2026. This year has six failures by September, about 0.67 a month, and the July-September pace was about 1.3 a month.
- The plain year-to-date pace would imply a Poisson mean of about 1.3 for the window. Historical year-end quietness pulls that down. I blend to a mean of about 0.9.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- 2026-09-25: Nano Banc was the sixth 2026 failure and the largest. Four failures came in July-September, so the pace is accelerating.
- 2026-08-25: The Problem Bank List fell by 7 to 47. Industry profits are strong and the DIF is healthy. Commentary calls the failures idiosyncratic, not systemic.
- 2026-10-27: Rates are 3.75-4.00% with a December hike possible, and Brent is near $117. This is mild added stress on small banks heavy in commercial real estate or securities.
- 2026-10-28: Manifold "7+ in 2026" is at 51%, implying about a 50% chance of at least one more failure by December 31. That includes October 30, so it is consistent with roughly 45-50% for the window itself. The Polymarket 0.74 window is unverified, so I treat it only as weak upward support.

(e) **Unexpected scenario:** A rate hike plus energy-driven credit stress could hit a cluster of small banks heavy in commercial real estate, producing 3 or more failures within weeks. Alternatively, the summer drip could simply stop, leaving 0.

I move from the historical base rate, about 80% for 0, toward the 2026 pace and the Manifold anchor. That gives about 42% for 0, with a Poisson-shaped tail.

Option_B: 0.35
Option_C: 0.16
Option_D: 0.07

(b) **Status quo:** As of October 28, no failure counts yet. If nothing changed, the answer would be 0.

(c) **Base rates:**
- In November-December of 2017-2025, there were 7 years with 0 failures, 2 years with 1, and no years with 2 or more.
- 2026 is running hotter than any of those years: 6 failures by late September, and 4 of them between July and September.
- The full-year 2026 pace of about 0.67 a month gives a mean of about 1.3 over two months.
- The recent July-September pace of about 1.3 a month would give about 2.6.
- Year-end seasonality pulls the other way, since late-December closures are rare.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- FDIC list (updated 2026-09-25): six failures in 2026, all small and idiosyncratic. The latest, Nano Banc (about $736M in assets), failed 2026-09-25.
- Q2 2026 Quarterly Banking Profile (2026-08-25): the Problem Bank List fell to 47 banks and industry earnings were strong. This points to no systemic wave.
- Macro backdrop (2026-10-27): the Fed is at 3.75-4.00% with a December hike possible, and oil is near $117. This adds tail stress for banks heavy in commercial real estate or securities.
- Manifold "7+ failures in 2026" is at 51%. That implies roughly a 50% chance of at least one failure between now and December 31, including October 30, which would not count. It is thinly traded.
- Polymarket is at 0.74 for "a failure by Dec 31," but its window is unclear. It probably starts sometime after September 25, so it is not directly comparable.

Taken together, a blended Poisson rate of about 0.85-0.9 for the November-December window seems reasonable. I moved up substantially from the historical November-December base rate (about 0.2) because of 2026's elevated pace. I stayed below a naive extrapolation of the recent pace because of year-end seasonality and the Manifold signal. I also added some overdispersion, since failures can cluster.

(e) **Unexpected scenario:** A December Fed hike plus commercial real estate losses could trigger a cluster of 3 or more small-bank closures in November and early December, similar to the July spacing of one week apart. Alternatively, regulators could hold off over the holidays and no bank fails at all, which is consistent with most recent years.

(b) **Status quo:** No failure in the window so far. If nothing changed, the answer would be "0". Zero failures in any given 2-month window is the historical norm in quiet years.

(c) **Base rates:**
- In the last 9 years, November-December had 0 failures 7 times and exactly 1 failure 2 times (2019 and 2023). No year had 2 or more.
- Those years were mostly quieter than 2026. 2026 has 6 failures by September, and 4 of them came in July to September.
- A Poisson model at the 2026 annual pace (about 0.67 a month) gives λ ≈ 1.3 for two months. The recent quarter's pace is higher.
- November-December is seasonally light, partly because of holidays and FDIC behaviour around year-end. That argues for a lower λ, around 0.8 to 1.0.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- The FDIC list was last updated 2026-09-25 with Nano Banc, the 6th failure of 2026 and the largest. No October failure has been reported.
- The Q2 QBP (2026-08-25) showed the Problem Bank List falling to 47 and the DIF healthy. This points to idiosyncratic small failures, not a wave.

- Polymarket at 0.74 has an unclear window, so I give it low weight.
- On the macro side, oil is near $117 and a December Fed hike is possible. This adds modest stress on banks heavy in commercial real estate or securities.

(e) **Unexpected scenario:** A rate shock or oil-driven credit stress exposes several small banks with concentrated commercial real estate or fraud problems. The FDIC then closes 2 or 3 banks across November and early December, much like the July clustering (failures on July 10 and July 17). Alternatively, the drip simply stops, as happened after October 2024, and the window ends with zero.

**Reasoning:** I start from a seasonally adjusted Poisson with λ ≈ 0.9: about 41% for 0, 37% for 1, 16% for 2 and 6% for 3+. The Manifold-implied chance of no further failure (about 49%, over a slightly wider window) suggests zero is a bit more likely than that. Historical November-December base rates also lean toward zero. Against this, failures can cluster, so I keep a fatter tail on 3+. Net effect: a small shift toward 0 and some extra weight on the tail.
